object_description: school complex of scattered volumes around a central square
design_condition: The existing building remains central within an east-west playground, while new volumes line the square and a surrounding green belt responds to the sloping topography and connects the complex to the district.

positive.statement: The proposal demonstrates a strong spatial idea and a precise urban setting of the buildings within the designed landscape.
The composition balances actively and passively usable spaces and creates atmospheric tension between built and natural open space.
The approach creates an extremely independent identity and transforms the site into an important open space for the district.
Despite the challenging topography, almost barrier-free access to all areas is offered.
The volumetric formation incorporates the scale and qualities of the existing building.
The organization and distribution of uses are well thought out and largely correspond to the client's ideas.
The planned phases enable seamless school operations.
The construction allows simple adjustments as user needs change and supports sustainability through material and structural robustness.
The clear operational arrangement of the teaching areas enables three clusters and usable corridor areas.
The arrangement of the auditorium, library, care and specialist rooms enables autonomous extracurricular use.

negative.statement: The chosen facade cladding is not convincing in terms of expression and sustainability.
The formal design of the entrance canopies is not yet convincing.
The internal development and organization are not yet convincing; access to the sports hall appears narrow and committed only to functionality.
The location of the bicycle shelter must be reconsidered because of its distance from the road and restrictions on civil-defense-system usability.
The long-term relocation of the kindergarten would affect operations that still need clarification.
The environmental design remains somewhat schematic and requires more differentiated elaboration.
The renovation work and its impact on the continued usability of the civil-defense facility still need to be proven.
